ai.headline: Google I/O 2026: Gemini 3.5 Flash GA, Gemini Spark 24/7 agent, Antigravity 2.0 agentic platform
ai.body: Gemini 3.5 Flash launches at GA (skipping preview), surpassing Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding, agent, and multimodal benchmarks at 4× speed and half the cost, with a notable price bump over prior Flash. Gemini Spark is a new 24/7 personal agent running on Google Cloud VMs that takes agentic actions across Workspace, Chrome, email, and chat. Antigravity 2.0 is a dedicated multi-agent orchestration platform supporting parallel autonomous agents, dynamic subagents, scheduled tasks, and artifacts — now GA on macOS. Token usage across Google AI systems reached 3.2 quadrillion/month; Gemini app hit 900M MAU.

ai.headline: Cloudflare Project Glasswing: Mythos AI model chains low-severity bugs into working exploits in internal codebase
ai.body: Cloudflare tested Anthropic's Mythos Preview against 50+ internal repos and observed it chaining use-after-free, arbitrary read/write, and ROP primitives into working PoC exploits, self-validating by compiling and running them in a scratch env. A purpose-built 8-stage harness (Recon→Report) outperformed generic coding agents by scoping parallel tasks to single attack classes with an adversarial second agent that cut false-positive hedging dominant in memory-unsafe-language scans. Key finding: model refusals are inconsistent across semantically equivalent prompts, and sub-two-hour patching SLAs backfire without regression testing — architectural mitigations (WAF reachability, intra-app isolation) are required complements.

ai.headline: Andrej Karpathy joins Anthropic for frontier R&D
ai.body: Karpathy announced he is joining Anthropic, citing the next few years at the LLM frontier as especially formative, signalling a return to core research rather than education. The move concentrates another top-tier AI researcher at Anthropic, intensifying competition with OpenAI and Google.

ai.headline: Netflix multimodal video search: three-stage pipeline fusing ensemble AI model outputs via temporal bucketing
ai.body: Netflix built a production video search system that ingests outputs from specialist models (character recognition, scene classification, dialogue transcription, object detection) into Cassandra, fuses them via one-second temporal bucketing with upsert semantics, then indexes enriched nested documents in Elasticsearch for hybrid text+vector queries at sub-second latency. The temporal bucketing design — composite key of asset ID + time bucket — handles incremental model additions and avoids duplicate records at scale (7.2M buckets per 2,000-hour archive). A parallel track is developing MediaFM, a unified foundation model for audio/video/text, but the ensemble pipeline remains the production system.

ai.headline: OpenAI Guaranteed Capacity: 1–3 year compute commitments with volume discounts
ai.body: OpenAI is offering enterprise customers pre-committed, long-term access to compute capacity (1-, 2-, 3-year terms) for running agents and AI workflows, with deeper discounts for longer terms. Supply is limited to current allocation; subsequent rounds will follow. This mirrors cloud reserved-instance pricing models and signals OpenAI positioning itself as infrastructure provider for agentic workloads.

sec.headline: CVE-2026-20182: CVSS 10.0 auth bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN enables unauthenticated control-plane compromise
sec.body: Rapid7 disclosed a critical DTLS session forgery flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN's vHub component allowing unauthenticated device authentication bypass and persistent unauthorized access to the SD-WAN control plane. Cisco has issued firmware patches; affected orgs should upgrade immediately and audit logs for suspicious DTLS activity. Any unpatched internet-exposed SD-WAN management plane should be treated as potentially compromised.

sec.headline: SHub Reaper macOS stealer: typosquatted Microsoft domain, bypasses Apple Tahoe 26.4 ClickFix, steals crypto wallets and RDP files
sec.body: SentinelOne identified a new SHub Stealer variant using fake WeChat/Miro installers from mlcrosoft[.]co[.]com that exploits the applescript:// URL scheme to bypass Apple's Tahoe 26.4 ClickFix mitigation, skips CIS-region hosts, and exfiltrates .docx/.wallet/.key/.json/.rdp files in 70MB chunks. It replaces Exodus, Atomic Wallet, Ledger Live, and Trezor Suite app.asar files with ad hoc code-signed payloads and installs a LaunchAgent backdoor masquerading as com.google.keystone.agent.plist beaconing every 60 seconds. Hunt indicators: unexpected osascript post-Script Editor, Google/Apple-namespaced LaunchAgents in ~/Library/Application Support/, outbound to hebsbsbzjsjshduxbs[.]xyz.

sec.headline: Drupal urgent core security updates shipped May 20 — exploit window is open
sec.body: Drupal released critical core patches for 11.x and 10.x branches on May 20; exploits are expected to emerge rapidly post-disclosure. Admins must apply the May 20 fixes on top of the latest branch minimums (11.3.x, 11.2.x, 10.6.x, 10.5.x); Drupal 7 is unaffected.

sec.headline: Datadog Pathfinding Labs: 100+ intentionally vulnerable AWS environments for CSPM and privilege-escalation testing
sec.body: Datadog open-sourced Pathfinding Labs, a Terraform-driven set of 100+ vulnerable AWS environments mapped to the pathfinding.cloud privilege escalation catalog, covering self-escalation, multi-hop, cross-account, and toxic-combination scenarios. Each lab ships with a scripted demo_attack.sh for repeatable exploitation via a plabs CLI (enable/apply/demo/destroy). Useful for validating CSPM tool coverage and training red/blue teams against realistic cloud misconfiguration patterns.

sec.headline: Inverting PhotoDNA: ML model reconstructs recognizable images from Microsoft's "irreversible" hash
sec.body: A researcher demonstrated that PhotoDNA hashes — long claimed to be non-invertible — leak sufficient image information for a machine learning model (Ribosome) to reconstruct visually recognizable images. This challenges the privacy and legal assumptions underpinning PhotoDNA's deployment across CSAM detection pipelines at scale.

swe.headline: Netflix multimodal video search architecture: Cassandra ingest → temporal bucket fusion → Elasticsearch nested-document index
swe.body: The production system decouples three concerns: high-throughput write ingestion to Cassandra (zero transformation), offline async fusion via one-second temporal bucketing with composite-key upserts, and Elasticsearch indexing of hierarchical parent/child documents for hybrid text+vector queries. This separation means complex cross-model intersection never contends with real-time ingestion. The 1-second bucket granularity was chosen as the precision/manageability tradeoff at Netflix's archive scale.

mkt.headline: Meta lays off ~8,000 (10% of workforce), pivots 7,000 staff to AI, closes 6,000 open roles; $145B AI capex committed for 2026
mkt.body: Meta began notifying ~8,000 employees of termination today; simultaneously 7,000 are being redeployed to AI initiatives and 6,000 open roles closed. The company is reporting record profits while committing up to $145B in 2026 AI spending, with an internal program tracking employee computer activity to train AI models on task completion patterns. This is the largest structural AI-driven workforce realignment at a major tech platform to date.

mkt.headline: SpaceX filing for IPO as soon as today (June 12 listing), plans to acquire Cursor AI coding tool in July with $10B breakup fee
mkt.body: SpaceX is expected to file its IPO paperwork today targeting a June 12 listing, with a concurrent plan to acquire AI coding startup Cursor in July. A $10B cash breakup fee is in place if the deal fails regulatory review. Cursor's acquisition by SpaceX would be a significant signal on enterprise AI tooling valuations and Big Tech's appetite for AI developer infrastructure.
